data.revised_prompt: The X-shaped skeleton layout of four intersecting arms and four circular motor mounts in <Picture 1> is <Subject 1>. The square top-down framing and scale in <Picture 1> is <Subject 2>. The target image transforms the flat diagram into a photorealistic 8K industrial design rendering of a quadcopter seen from a 90-degree overhead view, keeping the exact arm and mount positions of <Subject 1> within <Subject 2> while replacing the flat grey shapes with a detailed carbon-fiber airframe, fuselage, and propellers. <Subject 1> is partially preserved; the exact spatial placement, angles, and proportions of the four arms and four motor mounts are retained, while their flat grey 2D appearance changes into three-dimensional mechanical components. <Subject 2> is fully preserved. The quadcopter features a cold grey color scheme with a streamlined central fuselage having a 60-degree edge angle, anodized aluminum honeycomb grilles, and a discreetly integrated top-surface GPS antenna. Extending along the exact trajectories of <Subject 1> are foldable carbon-fiber arms with modular quick-release connectors, terminating at reinforced motor covers at the four original mount locations. Four ABS propellers with nano-coating are mounted over the motors, arranged with a 52-degree rotor angle and an 80-centimeter wing curvature radius, spanning a 30-centimeter rotor-to-rotor distance with a 1.3:1 arm span ratio. A glowing blue LED light band accents the body, and soft 5500K studio lighting casts high-contrast shadows across the matte dark background.
